title: Dust Emission in an Accretion-rate-limited Sample of z ≳ 6 Quasars
question: What are the FIR dust continuum properties of a UV luminosity-limited sample of z>6 quasar hosts, and does FIR luminosity (star formation) correlate with quasar UV luminosity (black hole growth)?

data.sensitivity: typical rms 0.5 mJy/beam in 30 km/s bins

what.value: Redshifts and M1450 of the sample quasars

evidence.quote: References for the redshift and $M_{1450}$: (1) (cite: dec18), (2) (cite: ban16)

what.value: Literature 1 mm flux densities, redshifts and M1450 of z>5.7 quasars (Table 3)

evidence.quote: From the literature we collected all available observations of high-redshift ($z>5.7$) quasars obtained in the 1 mm band.

external_data.citation: (cite: wan08b); (cite: omo13); (cite: wan13); (cite: ven16) and others

what.value: Dust mass opacity kappa = 0.77 (nu/352 GHz)^beta cm2/g

evidence.quote: we can fit templates of the local star-forming galaxies Arp 220 and M82 (cite: sil98)

recipe.method: Average line-free channels in [C II] windows (1900 GHz rest) and all channels in lower sideband windows (1790 GHz rest); for four faint sources average all line-free channels of four windows

recipe.goal: measure continuum flux densities and sizes
recipe.method: Peak pixel within 0.5 arcsec of quasar position; imfit integrated flux if peak S/N>=7, else peak flux

recipe.goal: derive FIR luminosity, SFR and dust mass
recipe.method: Scale modified blackbody to measured flux; integrate 42.5–122.5 um for L_FIR and 3–1100 um for L_TIR; SFR from Murphy relation; dust mass from Eq. 2
assumptions: T_dust=47 K, beta=1.6, negligible dust optical depth, Kroupa IMF, all dust heated by star formation

recipe.goal: test L_FIR vs UV luminosity correlation
recipe.method: Pearson correlation and straight-line fit of log L_FIR vs M1450 for all literature+new quasars and for the complete luminosity-limited sample

evidence.quote: $0.12<S_\mathrm{rest,\,1900\,GHz}<5.9$ mJy, with a median (mean) flux density of 0.88 mJy (1.59 mJy)
$L_{\mathrm{FIR}}$ $=(0.27-13)\times10^{12}$ $L_\ensuremath{\odot}$, with 74% of our quasar hosts having $L_{\mathrm{FIR}}$ $>10^{12}$ $L_\ensuremath{\odot}$
we derive SFRs of SFR $=50-2700$ $M_\ensuremath{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$
the estimated dust masses range from $M_\mathrm{dust} \approx 2\times10^7$ $M_\ensuremath{\odot}$ for the faintest sources

evidence.loc: 4.4 Correlation between the FIR and UV Luminosity
4.4 Correlation between the FIR and UV Luminosity
evidence.quote: the correlation is even weaker, with a Pearson’s $r=-0.22$

answer_key.quantity: Linear fit slope log L_FIR vs (M_UV+26)

evidence.loc: 4.4 Correlation between the FIR and UV Luminosity

not_stated_but_needed: Calibration pipeline, CASA version, calibrators and flux scale uncertainty (deferred to Decarli et al. 2018)
tclean parameters: weighting/robust, cell size, image size, masking, deconvolver
